questions.question: What is expense?
questions.solution_html:
• An expense is the cost incurred by a business in the process of earning revenue. It includes
  • payments for rent, salaries, electricity, and other operational activities. Expenses reduce the profit
  • of the business and are recorded in the Profit and Loss Account. Expenses can be classified as
  • direct expenses and indirect expenses.
  • A financial transaction is any business activity that involves the exchange of money or monetary
  • value. It includes purchases, sales, payments, and receipts. Every transaction affects the financial
  • position of the business. These are recorded in accounting books.
  • Speed and Accuracy
  • Computerized systems process transactions very quickly compared to manual methods.
  • Calculations are done automatically, reducing human errors and ensuring accurate
  • financial records.
  • Accounting Vouchers
  • These vouchers are used to record financial transactions
  • • Contra Voucher (F4): Records cash and bank transactions like deposits and withdrawals.
  • • Payment Voucher (F5): Used for payments made by the business.
  • • Receipt Voucher (F6): Used for money received.
  • • Journal Voucher (F7): Records adjustment entries such as depreciation and provisions.
  • Go to Gateway of Tally → Display → Day Book or select the relevant voucher register.

  • Outstanding salaries refer to salaries that are due but not yet paid at the end of the accounting
  • period. Since it is an expense incurred, it must be recorded.

questions.question: What is manual accounting?
questions.solution_html:
• Manual accounting is the traditional method of recording financial transactions by hand. It
  • involves maintaining physical books like journals and ledgers. It is time-consuming and prone to
  • errors. However, it helps in understanding basic accounting concepts.
  • Automation of Tasks
  • Routine tasks like ledger posting, calculations, and report generation are automated. This
  • reduces manual effort and saves time.
  • Importance
  • Altering transactions helps correct mistakes without deleting records. At the same time, proper
  • control measures ensure data integrity, prevent fraud, and maintain reliable financial
  • statements. Computerized accounting systems provide flexibility along with accuracy when
  • proper procedures and controls are followed.
questions.final_answer: proper procedures and controls are followed

questions.question: What is a ledger?
questions.solution_html:
• A ledger is a book or record that contains all accounts of a business. It classifies and summarizes
  • transactions recorded in the journal. Each account, such as cash or sales, has a separate ledger. It
  • helps in preparing financial statements.
  • Easy Reporting and Analysis
  • Various financial and inventory reports can be generated instantly. These reports help in
  • analyzing business performance and planning future strategies.
questions.final_answer: analyzing business performance and planning future strategies

questions.question: Describe the process of generating reports in Tally.
questions.solution_html:
• Tally provides a wide range of reports that help businesses analyze financial and inventory data
  • effectively. The process of generating reports is simple and user-friendly, enabling quick access
  • to important information.
  • To generate reports, go to the Gateway of Tally, which is the main menu. From there, select
  • the type of report required, such as Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Stock Summary
  • Cash Flow Statement, or Ledger Reports. Once selected, the report will be displayed instantly
  • with real-time data.
  • Tally also provides options to customize reports. By pressing F12 , users can
  • modify settings such as showing additional details, filtering specific data, or changing display
  • formats. The drill-down feature allows users to move from summary reports to detailed
  • transaction-level information by simply selecting an item.
  • Reports can also be exported, printed, or emailed for external use. For example, financial
  • statements can be shared with auditors or management. The ability to generate accurate and
  • timely reports helps in monitoring business performance, controlling costs, and making
  • informed decisions.
questions.final_answer: informed decisions

questions.question: What is a purchase voucher?
questions.solution_html:
• A Purchase Voucher is an accounting document used to record all purchase transactions of
  • goods or services in Tally. It plays a vital role in maintaining accurate purchase records and
  • updating inventory and accounts.
  • In Tally, a Purchase Voucher is created using F9 (Purchase Voucher). It records details such
  • as the supplier’s name, invoice number, date, quantity, rate, and total amount. It can be
  • recorded in two modes: Item Invoice Mode (affects both inventory and accounts) and
  • Accounting Invoice Mode (affects only accounts).
  • When goods are purchased, the purchase voucher increases the stock quantity and records the
  • liability towards the supplier. It also helps in calculating taxes such as GST automatically.
  • Purchase vouchers are important for tracking expenses, maintaining supplier records, and
  • preparing financial statements. They also help in verifying purchase transactions during audits.
  • Thus, a Purchase Voucher is an essential tool for recording and managing purchase activities
  • in a systematic and accurate manner.
questions.final_answer: in a systematic and accurate manner

questions.question: Describe the procedure for selecting and closing a company.
questions.solution_html:
• In Tally, selecting and closing a company are basic operations required for managing multiple
  • company accounts efficiently.
  • To select a company, go to Gateway of Tally → Select Company. A list of available
  • companies will be displayed. Choose the required company and press Enter. Once selected, the
  • company becomes active, and all transactions and reports will relate to that company.
questions.final_answer: company becomes active, and all transactions and reports will relate to that company

questions.question: Describe the procedure for creating, displaying, altering, and deleting Stock Items.
questions.solution_html:
• Procedure for Creating, Displaying, Altering, and Deleting Stock Items
  • Stock Items represent the goods handled by a business and are essential for inventory
  • management in Tally. Proper management of stock items ensures accurate tracking and
  • reporting.
  • To create a stock item, go to Gateway of Tally → Inventory Info → Stock Items → Create.
  • Enter details such as Name, Stock Group, Unit of Measurement, Rate, and Opening Balance
  • then save.
  • To display a stock item, go to Display → Inventory Books → Stock Item. This allows users to
  • view details without making any changes.
  • To alter a stock item, select Inventory Info → Stock Items → Alter, choose the item, make
  • necessary changes, and save.
  • To delete a stock item, open it in alter mode and press Alt + D. This will remove the item
  • permanently.
  • These functions help in maintaining accurate inventory records, updating information when
  • required, and ensuring smooth business operations.
  • Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Option (d) This will remove the item

questions.question: Describe the procedure for creating, displaying, altering, and deleting Stock Items.
questions.solution_html:

  • Stock Items represent the goods handled by a business and are essential for inventory
  • management in Tally. Proper management of stock items ensures accurate tracking and
  • reporting.
  • To create a stock item, go to Gateway of Tally → Inventory Info → Stock Items → Create.
  • Enter details such as Name, Stock Group, Unit of Measurement, Rate, and Opening Balance
  • then save.
  • To display a stock item, go to Display → Inventory Books → Stock Item. This allows users to
  • view details without making any changes.
  • To alter a stock item, select Inventory Info → Stock Items → Alter, choose the item, make
  • necessary changes, and save.
  • To delete a stock item, open it in alter mode and press Alt + D. This will remove the item
  • permanently.
  • These functions help in maintaining accurate inventory records, updating information when
  • required, and ensuring smooth business operations.
